llm.summary: This memory skill is mostly purpose-aligned, but it broadly preserves full conversation content and can sync archives to a hard-coded NAS, so users should review it carefully before installing.

dimensions.detail: Local file access is expected for a file-backed memory system, but the NAS sync script uses fixed IPs, user, SSH key path, and target path, and some scripts ignore the documented OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE setting.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is manual symlinking into PATH and session-start instructions; no install-time execution was found, but referenced tools such as auto_log, memory_search, memcheck, and session-dumper are not included in the inspected artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions tell the agent to read memory before answering and log after every interaction, with no built-in per-message consent, redaction, retention limit, or review gate before old context is resurfaced.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact stores plaintext daily logs, decisions, mesh data, checkpoints, session wraps, and verbatim PDFs, then may duplicate them to remote storage without built-in deletion or sensitivity controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's memory, logging, search, checkpoint, PDF archive, and NAS-sync capabilities fit its stated purpose, but they capture and retain high-sensitivity conversation data at full fidelity.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intentionally want long-lived plaintext memory of agent interactions. Do not use it with passwords, tokens, private keys, regulated data, or confidential work unless you add redaction, retention, and access controls. Review or remove the NAS sync script and clarify/disable any session-dumper cron before use.
llm.findings:
[TT2] unexpected: Decision files are expected, but the topic-derived filename only lowercases and replaces spaces, so path scoping is weak even if practical overwrite depends on existing intermediate directories.
[LP3] expected: Shell and file read/write behavior are expected for this memory skill, but the manifest does not clearly declare a permissions boundary or precise paths.
[TP4] expected: I did not validate hidden purpose for auto-logging, PDF archival, NAS sync, or session dumping because SKILL.md discloses them; the remaining concern is under-scoped hard-coded NAS sync and sparse checkpoint retention detail.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The README says there is no background daemon while also documenting a five-minute session-dumper cron; no cron installer was present, but the documentation conflict is material.
[SDI-1] expected: Checkpoint storage is purpose-aligned and referenced by the docs, but it stores raw context and extras as plaintext and resume can write that context into today.md without review.
[SQP-2] expected: Logging, PDF archival, and NAS sync are disclosed, but they preserve full interactions and durable plaintext copies without built-in redaction or per-message consent.
[SSD-3] expected: Persistent memory and resurfacing are core features; the concern is breadth across logs, checkpoints, decisions, wraps, PDFs, and remote sync.
[RA2] expected: Session persistence is the stated purpose, not rogue behavior by itself, but it contributes to Review because the skill strongly encourages use before and after every interaction.
